content.text: Digital creators in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, and other regions where Stripe is unavailable face infrastructure challenges. Many rely on workarounds like manual payment verification or centralized platforms that lock them out. COREMERCH's Sovereign Blueprint offers a solution, enabling digital stores to operate independently with [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/supabase-order-database-digital-stores-which-architecture-actually|Supabase as]] as the order database, no stripe required. By [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/deploying-digital-store-cloudflare-pages-free-step-step-7|deploying]] Stack 01 or Stack 02, creators can host their stores on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, use Cloudflare Workers or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/google-apps-script-digital-commerce-automation-what-actually-9|COREMERCH guide to google]] Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic crypto payment verification. This guide explains how to set up a digital store with supabase as the order database, deploying Stack 01 in 4-6 hours following the Sovereign Blueprint.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

Supabase serves as a decentralized order database, allowing digital stores to operate independently from Stripe or other centralized platforms. This architecture ensures creators retain full control over their data, even when platforms fail or impose restrictions. With supabase, creators can configure custom payment and delivery pipelines, making it possible to accept crypto payments directly from customers. This approach eliminates the need for workarounds or manual payment verification, providing a seamless and secure experience for both creators and customers.
What You Need Before You Deploy

To deploy a digital store with supabase as the order database, you need to have a GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages account, a NOWPayments account, and the Sovereign Blueprint. You should also have a basic understanding of Google Apps Script or Cloudflare Workers for backend logic. This guide assumes you have a digital product to sell, such as an ebook or course, and a clear understanding of your target audience and pricing strategy.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

The NOWPayments configuration sequence is the same regardless of which stack you are deploying. Create a NOWPayments account — no KYC required, no document upload, no bank account needed. Navigate to the wallet settings and add the wallet addresses for each cryptocurrency you want to accept. USDT on Tron and Bitcoin are the practical starting point for most creators in restricted markets. Generate an API key from the NOWPayments dashboard. Set the webhook endpoint URL in the NOWPayments IPN settings pointing to your Cloudflare Worker or Apps Script Web App. Set the webhook secret key — a string you generate that both NOWPayments and your backend know.
Deploying Stack 01 in 4-6 hours following the Sovereign Blueprint enables digital creators to build a scalable and secure infrastructure for their digital stores.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Testing before promotion is not optional — it is the step that determines whether your store functions correctly under real conditions before real buyers encounter it. The test sequence has four steps. First: deploy the backend and confirm the webhook endpoint returns a valid response to a test HTTP POST. Second: configure the storefront and confirm the checkout displays correctly on desktop and mobile. Third: complete a real mainnet transaction with a small amount of actual crypto. Fourth: check your order database and confirm the order was logged correctly, the delivery email arrived, and the download link works.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The post-deployment ownership transfer is explicit in every COREMERCH deployment. When the build is complete and the end-to-end test passes, COREMERCH provides the credentials and configuration details for every component under the customer's accounts. The GitHub or Cloudflare repository is under the customer's account from the start. The Supabase or Google Sheets database is under the customer's account. The NOWPayments account is under the customer's email. COREMERCH removes collaborator access upon delivery. From that point, the store runs entirely under the customer's own accounts.

Link your supabase database to your store frontend. Set up Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. Test your store on mainnet and process your first transaction. Monitor your store's performance and optimize your payment and delivery pipeline. Upgrade to Stack 02 for more advanced features and end-to-end testing.
